translation.proposed_text_en:
(1) Income from employment (wages) is: 
1. a) emoluments and benefits from an existing or former employment relationship. 
b) emoluments and benefits of persons who are not substantially interested in corporations within the meaning of Section 22 no. 2, even if, in the case of an employment which otherwise exhibits all the characteristics of an employment relationship (Section 47(2)), the obligation to follow the instructions of another is absent on the basis of a special provision in the articles of association. 
c) emoluments from a statutory sickness or accident insurance. 
d) emoluments from a foreign statutory sickness or accident insurance which corresponds to a domestic sickness or accident insurance. 
e) sickness benefits from the welfare and support institutions of the chambers of self-employed persons.
issues: The content of Sections 22 no. 2 and 47(2) is not supplied.

translation.proposed_text_en:
A business trip occurs when an employee

— leaves their duty station (office, permanent establishment, factory premises, warehouse, etc.) on the employer’s orders to perform work duties, or
— works so far away from their permanent place of residence (family home) that they cannot reasonably be expected to return to that permanent place of residence (family home) on a daily basis.
